headline: The Rugby Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a rugby skill and check it with a teach-back, refuse an unsafe return to play, settle a dressing-room conflict, run a 112 emergency call at training, and write the weekly report in Spanish.

lessons.title: Teach a New Scrum-Half Our Exit from the 22
lessons.objective: Explain step by step how and why the team exits its own 22, then have the new scrum-half teach it back.

words.note: Many players in Spain just say 'el box kick'.
Usual term in Spain for a rugby penalty.

words.en: First the nine looks, then we kick to touch.
words.es: Primero el nueve mira, luego pateamos a touch.

words.en: We don't run from here because a turnover costs us points.
words.es: No corremos desde aquí porque una pérdida nos cuesta puntos.

words.en: That's why we kick long and all move up together.
words.es: Por eso pateamos largo y subimos todos juntos.

words.en: I get that you ran more in Uruguay, but here we play like this.
words.es: Entiendo que en Uruguay corrían más, pero aquí jugamos así.

words.en: Outside our 22, you can run if you see a gap.
words.es: Fuera de nuestra 22, puedes correr si ves hueco.
words.note: In Spain people say 'la 22' (feminine).

words.en: Why do we kick and not run?
Now you explain it to me, step by step.
words.es: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso a paso.
words.note: Informal (tú), coach to player.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Tomás, a new scrum-half: explain the club's exit from the 22 step by step using primero, luego, porque and por eso, then have him teach the plan back to you.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso: primero el nueve mira, luego pateamos, por eso no corremos)

examples.es: Primero el nueve mira la defensa, luego pateamos a touch.
examples.en: First the nine looks at the defence, then we kick to touch.

examples.es: Perder el balón aquí es ensayo seguro; por eso no corremos.
examples.en: Losing the ball here is a sure try for them; that's why we don't run.

lessons.title: Read the Federation's New Tackle-Height Rule
lessons.objective: Read the federation's community tackle-height rule aloud and explain to young players what changes and why.

words.note: The youth and grassroots age groups.

words.en: According to the federation's rules, you tackle below the waist.
words.es: Según el reglamento de la federación, se tacklea bajo la cintura.

words.en: If the head is up high, there's more risk of concussion.
words.es: Si la cabeza va arriba, hay más riesgo de conmoción.

words.en: If the tackle is high, a penalty is given.
words.es: Si el tackle es alto, se cobra penal.

words.en: You bend at the waist before contact, not after.
words.es: Se dobla la cintura antes del contacto, no después.

words.en: Lucas, Noa, what changes for you in the tackle?
words.es: Lucas, Noa, ¿qué cambia para ustedes en el tackle?

words.en: Look, Pilar, the rule changed to protect the head.
words.es: Mire, Pilar, la norma cambió para proteger la cabeza.
words.note: Formal (usted) with a parent.

words.en: Do you have any other questions about the circular?
words.es: ¿Tiene alguna otra duda sobre la circular?
words.note: Formal (usted).

lessons.speaking: You are the under-16 coach, and the AI is Pilar, a volunteer parent: read the federation's tackle-height circular aloud and explain what changes and why, using impersonal se (se placa) and si + present (si la cabeza va arriba, hay más riesgo).

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se tackea más bajo; si la cabeza va arriba, hay más riesgo)

examples.es: En el rugby juvenil se tacklea más bajo, según el reglamento de la federación.
examples.en: In youth rugby you tackle lower, according to the federation's rules.

examples.es: Si el tackleador va erguido, hay más choques de cabezas.
examples.en: If the tackler is upright, there are more head clashes.

lessons.title: Train a Prop to Lift in the Lineout
lessons.objective: Coach a new lifter on grip, timing and safe lowering, correct him live, and have him teach it back.

words.en: Hold him by the upper thigh, not by the knee.
words.es: Sujétalo por la parte alta del muslo, no por la rodilla.

words.en: Grab him by the shorts, just below the glute.
words.es: Agárralo del pantalón corto, justo debajo del glúteo.

words.en: Lower him slowly until his feet are on the ground.
words.es: Bájalo despacio hasta que tenga los pies en el suelo.

words.en: Never let go of him before he touches the ground!
words.es: ¡No lo sueltes nunca antes de que toque el suelo!

words.en: Easy, Iker, you learn this by repeating it.
words.es: Tranquilo, Iker, esto se aprende repitiendo.
words.note: Informal (tú), supportive tone.

words.en: Samuel, tell us if you feel unsafe up there.
words.es: Samuel, avísanos si te sientes inseguro arriba.

words.en: Now you show me: where do you grip him and when do you let go?
words.es: Ahora enséñamelo tú: ¿dónde lo agarras y cuándo lo sueltas?

lessons.speaking: You are the forwards coach, and the AI is Iker, a prop learning to lift: coach his grip, timing and safe lowering on the mat with commands like sujétalo, bájalo despacio and no lo sueltes, then have him teach it back.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (sujétalo, bájalo despacio, no lo sueltes)

examples.es: Sujétalo fuerte y súbelo con las piernas, no con la espalda.
examples.en: Hold him tight and lift him with your legs, not your back.

examples.es: Bájalo despacio y no lo sueltes hasta el suelo.
examples.en: Lower him slowly and don't let go of him until he's on the ground.

lessons.title: Brief the Squad on a Tournament Heat Protocol
lessons.objective: Read a tournament heat protocol and brief the squad on water breaks, warning signs and who to tell.

words.en: Before warming up, everyone has to drink water.
words.es: Antes de calentar, hay que beber agua, todos.

words.en: You have to drink before you get thirsty.
words.es: Hay que beber antes de tener sed.

words.en: According to the tournament protocol, from 35 degrees there are extra breaks.
words.es: Según el protocolo del torneo, desde 35 grados hay pausas extra.

words.en: After playing, everyone into the shade and drink.
words.es: Después de jugar, todos a la sombra y a beber.

words.en: Before going out on the pitch, put on sunscreen.
words.es: Antes de salir al campo, pónganse crema solar.

words.en: If anyone feels dizzy or confused, tell the medical service right away, and if the person doesn’t respond, call 112.
words.es: Si alguien se marea o se confunde, avisen al servicio médico enseguida, y si no responde, llamen al 112.

words.en: Rocío, you make sure nobody skips the breaks.
words.es: Rocío, tú vigilas que nadie se salte las pausas.
words.note: Informal (tú) with the captain.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Rocío, the captain: go through the tournament heat protocol on water breaks, warning signs and who to tell, using antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que, and quote times as según el protocolo del torneo.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de calentar hay que beber; después de jugar, a la sombra)

examples.es: Antes de calentar hay que beber, según el protocolo del torneo.
examples.en: Before warming up you have to drink, according to the tournament protocol.

examples.es: Después de cada partido, hay que ir a la sombra y refrescarse.
examples.en: After each match, you have to go into the shade and cool down.

lessons.title: The Physio Finds a Hidden Hamstring Injury
lessons.objective: Find out what the player hid and when, then propose a safe plan for Saturday's selection.

words.note: Often plural: los isquiotibiales, for the muscle group.
Short form in the club: la fisio. Male: el fisioterapeuta.
Feminine noun that takes el in the singular: el alta médica, las altas.

words.en: Andrés, how long had your hamstring been hurting?
words.es: Andrés, ¿desde cuándo te dolía el isquiotibial?
words.note: Informal tú with a player. Imperfect for an ongoing past state.

words.en: Did it hurt when you ran or only when stretching?
words.es: ¿Te dolía cuando corrías o solo al estirar?

words.en: On Tuesday you stopped in the last sprint; what did you feel?
words.es: El martes paraste en el último sprint; ¿qué notaste?
words.note: Preterite for one finished action: paraste, notaste.

words.en: Ane, what did you find in the examination?
words.note: Informal tú between staff colleagues.

words.en: I understand you wanted to play the derby, but not like this.
words.es: Entiendo que querías jugar el derbi, pero no así.

words.en: I wouldn't pick you on Saturday; I'd rather wait for the scan.
words.es: Yo no te convocaría el sábado; prefiero esperar a la ecografía.

words.en: In your judgment, when could he return to contact training?
words.es: ¿Cuándo podría volver a entrenar con contacto, según tu criterio?

words.en: Next time, tell me on day one; nobody loses their place.
words.es: La próxima vez, dímelo el primer día; nadie pierde su puesto.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is lock Andrés Molina after physio Ane's report: find out what hurt and since when with the preterite and imperfect (te dolía cuando corrías, ayer paraste), then propose a safe plan for Saturday with the conditional (yo no te convocaría).

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (te dolía cuando corrías; ayer paraste; yo propondría que descanses)

examples.es: Te dolía cuando corrías, pero ayer paraste en seco.
examples.en: It hurt when you ran, but yesterday you pulled up sharply.

examples.es: Yo propondría un entrenamiento adaptado hasta la ecografía.
examples.en: I would propose modified training until the scan.

lessons.title: Two Props Down: Reshuffle the Front Row
lessons.objective: Compare the options when two props are injured and explain the plan without putting an untrained player at prop.

words.note: Usually plural in the rules: scrums no disputados.
Spain usage; Latin America says la banca.
Common in Spain; also el tercera línea ala.
Feminine noun that takes el: el acta, las actas.

words.en: Hugo, thanks for offering, but you're not going to play prop.
words.es: Hugo, te lo agradezco, pero no vas a jugar de pilar.
words.note: Informal tú with a teammate.

words.en: Bruno Castaño is stepping up; he's registered and trains in the front row.
words.es: Va a subir Bruno Castaño; tiene ficha y entrena en primera línea.

words.en: With Bruno it's safer than improvising with a flanker.
words.es: Con Bruno es más seguro que improvisar con un flanker.

words.en: Without props, there will be uncontested scrums, according to the competition rules.
words.es: Sin pilares, habrá scrums no disputados, según el reglamento de la competición.

words.en: We'll have fewer options on the bench, but nobody risks their neck.
words.es: Tendremos menos opciones en la banca, pero nadie se juega el cuello.
words.note: Jugarse el cuello means to risk your neck, and here it is literal too.

words.en: Joan, will you explain it to the forwards?
words.es: Joan, ¿se lo explicas tú a los delanteros?
words.note: Informal tú with the captain.

words.en: Hugo is going to play flanker, which is where he helps us most.
words.es: Hugo va a jugar de flanker, que es donde más nos ayuda.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is captain Joan Ferrer: explain who will cover prop and why, compare the options with más seguro que and menos, and set out the plan with the future and ir a (va a jugar Bruno, tendremos menos banquillo).

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (va a jugar Bruno; es más seguro que improvisar; tendremos menos banquillo)

examples.es: El sábado va a jugar Bruno de pilar derecho.
examples.en: On Saturday Bruno is going to play tighthead prop.

examples.es: Tendremos menos banca, pero es más seguro que improvisar.
examples.en: We'll have a shorter bench, but it's safer than improvising.

lessons.title: Citing Commissioner Questions Your Prop's Tackle
lessons.objective: Narrate a disputed tackle in order, giving the exact minute, shirt numbers, score and position on the pitch.

words.note: Male: el comisario de citaciones.

words.en: In minute 63, at 17-20, they attacked down the blind side.
words.es: En el minuto 63, con 17-20, atacaron por el lado cerrado.
words.note: Read the score aloud as diecisiete a veinte.

words.en: It was 5 metres from our line, next to touch.
words.es: Fue a 5 metros de nuestra línea, junto a la touch.

words.en: First number 12 arrived with the ball and then Martín went in.
words.es: Primero llegó el 12 con el balón y después entró Martín.

words.en: Could you play minute 63 again, please?
words.es: ¿Puede poner otra vez el minuto 63, por favor?
words.note: Formal usted with the commissioner.

words.en: Martín, just tell what happened, in order.
words.es: Martín, cuenta solo lo que pasó, en orden.
words.note: Informal tú with your player.

words.en: The referee didn't show a card and play went on.
words.es: El árbitro no sacó tarjeta y el juego siguió.

words.en: We're cooperating with the committee; we don't want to hide anything.
words.es: Colaboramos con el comité; no queremos esconder nada.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is citing commissioner Elena Villar: narrate the tackle in order with the preterite (entró, cayó, siguió), giving the exact minute, shirt numbers, score and spot on the pitch (en el minuto 63, con 17-20).

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (en el minuto 63, con 17-20, el número 3 entró y el 12 cayó)

examples.es: En el minuto 63, con 17-20, el número 3 entró y el 12 cayó.
examples.en: In minute 63, at 17-20, number 3 went in and number 12 fell.

examples.es: Martín tackleó con el hombro y el jugador cayó de espaldas.
examples.en: Martín tackled with his shoulder and the player fell on his back.

lessons.title: Saying No: A Father Wants His Son Back On
lessons.objective: Refuse a parent's demand to return a player after a head knock, give the reason and offer the next steps.

words.note: Always plural in Spanish.
Spain says urgencias; llevar a urgencias means take to the ER.

words.en: Mr Sanz, I understand you're worried about Diego.
words.es: Señor Sanz, entiendo que esté preocupado por Diego.
words.note: Formal usted with a parent.

words.en: Please don't insist; the decision belongs to the tournament doctor.
words.es: No insista, por favor; la decisión es del médico del torneo.
words.note: Formal negative command: no + usted subjunctive.

words.en: The doctor removed him under the federation's protocol.
words.es: El médico lo retiró según el protocolo de la federación.

words.en: After a head knock, I don't recommend he plays again today.
words.es: Con un golpe en la cabeza, no recomiendo que juegue más hoy.

words.en: Don't leave him alone tonight and watch for symptoms.
words.es: No lo deje solo esta noche y vigile los síntomas.

words.en: If he has nausea, vomiting, blurred vision or is very drowsy, take him to the ER or call 112.
words.es: Si tiene náuseas, vómito, visión borrosa o mucho sueño, llévelo a urgencias o llame al 112.

words.en: Javi, don't put him on even if his father insists.
words.es: Javi, no lo metas aunque el padre insista.
words.note: Informal tú with your assistant coach.

words.en: We'll talk tomorrow and I'll explain the graduated return.
words.es: Mañana hablamos y le explico la vuelta progresiva.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Ricardo Sanz, Diego's father: calmly refuse to send Diego back on, explain the doctor's decision under the protocol and give clear next steps, using negative commands (no insista) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no lo metas, no insista; no recomiendo que vuelva hoy)

examples.es: No recomiendo que vuelva hoy, aunque diga que está bien.
examples.en: I don't recommend that he goes back on today, even if he says he's fine.

examples.es: No lo metas en la semifinal; ya está fuera según el protocolo.
examples.en: Don't put him in for the semifinal; he's already out under the protocol.

lessons.title: Feedback to a Fly-Half Who Ignores the Calls
lessons.objective: Give specific feedback on ignored calls, recommend changes, and have the player teach back the new routine.

words.note: Common in Uruguay and Argentina for feedback on performance.
Cantar la jugada = to call the play out loud.

words.en: You ignored three backline calls in the second half.
words.es: Ignoraste tres llamadas de la línea en el segundo tiempo.

words.en: I want you to look at the nine before every exit.
words.es: Quiero que mires al nueve antes de cada salida.
words.note: Querer que + subjunctive: mires, not miras.

words.en: I recommend you confirm the play with the nine.
words.es: Te recomiendo que confirmes la jugada con el nueve.

words.en: I understand the forwards didn't help, but let's talk about your decisions.
words.es: Entiendo que los forwards no ayudaron, pero hablemos de tus decisiones.
words.note: Forwards and backs are standard rugby words in Uruguay and Argentina.

words.en: If you want to change something, I'd rather you tell me first.
words.es: Si quieres cambiar algo, prefiero que me lo digas antes.

words.en: I'm not looking for someone to blame; I want us to improve together.
words.es: No busco culpables; busco que mejoremos juntos.

words.en: Now you tell me the new routine, step by step.
words.es: Cuéntame tú la rutina nueva, paso a paso.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is fly-half Felipe Aguirre: give specific feedback on the three ignored backline calls, recommend changes with quiero que and te recomiendo que plus the subjunctive, and have him teach back the new routine.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (quiero que mires al nueve; te recomiendo que hables antes)

examples.es: Quiero que mires al nueve antes de pedir la pelota.
examples.en: I want you to look at the nine before calling for the ball.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que hables con los centros antes del partido.
examples.en: I recommend you talk to the centres before the match.

lessons.title: Settle a Row Between the Captain and a Senior Lock
lessons.objective: Report what each player said, set out the background, and agree on how lineout calls will be made.

words.note: Everyday Argentine rugby word for the lineout.
Argentine word for the home fans.

words.en: Julián, Gastón, lower your voices and sit down for a moment.
words.es: Julián, Gastón, bajen la voz y siéntense un momento.
words.note: Ustedes commands for the two players.

words.en: Julián said you changed the play at the last lineout.
words.es: Julián dijo que vos cambiaste la jugada en el último line.
words.note: Vos is normal in Buenos Aires; cambiaste is the same form as with tú.

words.en: Gastón, you said you couldn't hear him because of the noise.
words.es: Gastón, vos dijiste que no lo escuchabas por el ruido.

words.en: The crowd was shouting and nobody could hear the call properly.
words.es: La hinchada gritaba y nadie oía bien la llamada.

words.en: Each of you tells your side, without interrupting.
words.es: Cada uno cuenta su parte, sin interrumpir.

words.en: Do you agree that only Julián calls the lineout?
words.es: ¿Están de acuerdo en que solo Julián cante el line?

words.en: If there's any doubt, we use the agreed gesture, not shouting.
words.es: Si hay dudas, usamos el gesto acordado, no gritos.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is captain Julián Ríos and lock Gastón Pereyra: report what each said with dijo que, set out the background with the imperfect (soplaba, gritaba), and get them to agree on how lineout calls will be made.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (dijo que no lo escuchabas; el viento soplaba y la grada gritaba)

examples.es: Julián dijo que Gastón cambiaba la llamada a último momento.
examples.en: Julián said Gastón was changing the call at the last moment.

examples.es: El viento soplaba fuerte y la hinchada gritaba sin parar.
examples.en: The wind was blowing hard and the crowd was shouting nonstop.

lessons.title: Keep the Squad Going After Four Straight Losses
lessons.objective: Rally a losing squad with concrete commitments and convince a discouraged winger to stay.

words.note: Informal; tener un bajón = to be feeling down.
Always plural: tener ganas de seguir = to want to keep going.

words.en: Girls, this week we'll train tackling together.
words.es: Chicas, esta semana entrenaremos el tackle juntas.
words.note: Juntas, feminine, for a women's squad.

words.en: We're going to do it, but step by step.
words.es: Lo vamos a lograr, pero paso a paso.

words.en: We'll set ourselves small goals, one per match.
words.es: Nos marcaremos objetivos pequeños, uno por partido.

words.en: Four defeats don't erase everything we've improved.
words.es: Cuatro derrotas no borran todo lo que hemos mejorado.

words.en: Marta, you can do it; I've seen you grow this season.
words.es: Marta, tú puedes; te he visto crecer esta temporada.
words.note: Informal tú, coach to one player in Spain.

words.en: Before you decide anything, give me two more weeks.
words.es: Antes de decidir nada, dame dos semanas más.

words.en: I'll talk with you every Friday after training.
words.es: Hablaré contigo cada viernes después del entrenamiento.

words.en: What do you need from me to keep going?

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is winger Marta Gil and then the squad: rally the team with concrete commitments in the future (entrenaremos, hablaré) and vamos a + infinitive, encourage with tú puedes, and convince Marta to stay.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (entrenaremos el placaje juntos; lo vamos a lograr; tú puedes)

examples.es: El jueves entrenaremos el tackle juntas, una a una.
examples.en: On Thursday we'll train tackling together, one by one.

examples.es: Lo vamos a lograr, Marta; tú puedes con esto.
examples.en: We're going to do it, Marta; you can handle this.

lessons.title: Club Day: Referee, President, Teen and Sponsor
lessons.objective: Switch between usted and tú and soften requests for four listeners at one club event.

words.note: Spanish youth age category, the one just below juvenil.

words.en: Alberto, I wanted to thank you for refereeing this morning.
words.es: Alberto, quería agradecerle el arbitraje de esta mañana.
words.note: Formal (usted); quería softens the opening.

words.en: Carmen, I'd like to talk to you about the youth academy budget.
words.es: Carmen, quisiera comentarle el presupuesto de las divisiones formativas.
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: Would you mind reviewing this proposal before Friday?
words.es: ¿Le importaría revisar esta propuesta antes del viernes?
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: Hey, Pablo, you tackled really well today.
words.es: Oye, Pablo, hoy tackleaste muy bien.
words.note: Informal (tú), coach to a teenager.

words.en: Can you give me a hand with the cones?
words.es: ¿Me echas una mano con los conos?
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: Sergio, is it all right if I show you the facilities?
words.es: Sergio, ¿le parece bien si le enseño las instalaciones?
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: Your logo will go on the youth academy kits.
words.es: Su logotipo irá en los uniformes de las divisiones formativas.
words.note: Formal (usted).

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI plays referee Alberto Cuesta, president Carmen Robledo, 15-year-old Pablo Rey and sponsor rep Sergio Llorente in turn: thank, ask, encourage and brief each one, switching usted and tú and softening with quisiera, ¿le importaría? and ¿me echas una mano?

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿le importaría?, oye, ¿me echas una mano?)

examples.es: Carmen, ¿le importaría reunirse conmigo el lunes?
examples.en: Carmen, would you mind meeting with me on Monday?

examples.es: Oye, Pablo, ¿me echas una mano con las bolsas?
examples.en: Hey, Pablo, can you give me a hand with the bags?

lessons.title: Write the Incident Report for a Collapsed Scrum
lessons.objective: Narrate a scrum injury in time order for the official report: who did what, when, and the result.

words.note: Verb form: el scrum se hundió (the scrum collapsed).
A woman is la testigo.

words.en: At 17:42, the scrum collapsed with Raúl underneath.
words.es: A las 17:42, el scrum se hundió con Raúl debajo.

words.en: At that moment, the referee stopped the match.
words.es: En ese momento, el árbitro paró el partido.

words.en: Meanwhile, Inés was holding his head without moving him.
words.es: Mientras tanto, Inés le sujetaba la cabeza sin moverlo.
words.note: Imperfect (sujetaba) for the background action, preterite for events.

words.en: Two minutes later, Raúl said he felt tingling in his arms.
words.es: Dos minutos después, Raúl dijo que sentía hormigueo en los brazos.

words.en: The ambulance arrived at 18:05 and left for the hospital.
words.es: La ambulancia llegó a las 18:05 y salió hacia el hospital.

words.en: Inés, I have 17:50; what time did you write down?
words.es: Inés, yo tengo las 17:50; ¿tú qué hora apuntaste?
words.note: Informal: tú with a club colleague.

words.en: We'll put your time, because you were beside him.
words.es: Ponemos tu hora, porque tú estabas a su lado.

words.en: In the report we only put what we saw, no guesses.
words.es: En el informe solo ponemos lo que vimos, sin suposiciones.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Inés Moreno, the club first-aider: build the federation report of Raúl's injury minute by minute, saying who did what and when, with a las 17:42, en ese momento, dos minutos después and mientras tanto.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las 17:42, en ese momento, dos minutos después, mientras tanto)

examples.es: A las 17:42, el scrum se hundió y Raúl no se levantó.
examples.en: At 17:42, the scrum collapsed and Raúl didn't get up.

examples.es: Mientras tanto, yo llamé a la ambulancia desde la banda.
examples.en: Meanwhile, I called the ambulance from the touchline.

lessons.title: Near Miss: A Goalpost Nearly Falls on the Minis
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss without blame, say what could have happened, and agree on the change.

words.note: Common in Spanish safety talk; also el incidente sin daños.
Spanish club age group for children of about ten and eleven.
A woman is la encargada de mantenimiento.

words.en: The posts very nearly fell on the minis.
words.es: Por poco se caen los palos encima de los alevines.

words.en: It could have hit a child on the head.
words.es: Podría haber golpeado a un niño en la cabeza.

words.en: Nobody's to blame here; let's see what we change.
words.es: Aquí nadie tiene la culpa; vemos qué cambiamos.

words.en: If we anchor them per the manufacturer's instructions, they don't move.
words.es: Si los anclamos según las instrucciones del fabricante, no se mueven.

words.en: Paco, how many counterweights does the manufacturer require for these posts?
words.es: Paco, ¿cuántos contrapesos pide el fabricante para estos palos?
words.note: Informal: tú with a club colleague.

words.en: Laura, did you have time to move the kids away?
words.es: Laura, ¿les dio tiempo a apartar a los niños?

words.en: If there are strong gusts, we keep the kids away from the posts.
words.es: Si hay rachas fuertes, alejamos a los niños de los palos.

words.en: From now on, we check the anchoring before every training session.
words.es: A partir de ahora, revisamos el anclaje antes de cada entrenamiento.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Paco Lozano, the groundsman: talk through the goalpost that nearly fell without blaming anyone, say what could have happened with por poco and podría haber, and agree on anchoring it según las instrucciones del fabricante using si clauses.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco cae; podría haber golpeado a un niño; si lo anclamos, no se mueve)

examples.es: Por poco cae sobre el grupo de Laura.
examples.en: It very nearly fell on Laura's group.

examples.es: Si ponemos los contrapesos que pide el fabricante, no se vuelca.
examples.en: If we use the counterweights the manufacturer requires, it doesn't tip over.

lessons.title: A Player Collapses at Training: Call 112
lessons.objective: Call 112, pass on the operator's instructions, and give short commands to send for the defibrillator and guide the ambulance in.

words.note: Often called el DEA (desfibrilador externo automático).
Said letter by letter: erre, ce, pe.
A woman is la operadora.
Poner el altavoz: put the phone on speaker.

words.en: A player has collapsed and isn't responding.
words.es: Un jugador se ha desplomado y no responde.
words.note: Formal call to 112; Spain uses the present perfect for what just happened.

words.en: We're at the rugby pitch, next to the car park gate.
words.es: Estamos en el campo de rugby, junto a la puerta del aparcamiento.

words.en: I'm putting you on speaker to follow your instructions.
words.es: Pongo el altavoz para seguir sus instrucciones.
words.note: Formal: usted with the operator.

words.en: Unai, to the gate, and bring the ambulance over here!
words.es: ¡Unai, a la puerta, y trae a la ambulancia hasta aquí!

words.en: If he isn't breathing, I'll start compressions the way you tell me.
words.es: Si no respira, empiezo las compresiones como usted me diga.

words.en: Iratxe, switch it on and do what the device says.
words.es: Iratxe, enciéndelo y haz lo que diga el aparato.

words.en: Everyone else, step back and give us room!

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is the 112 operator: report that Óscar has collapsed, give your location, relay the operator's instructions using si + present → future, and shout short commands to Iratxe and Unai like ¡tú, el desfibrilador! and ¡tú, a la puerta!

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short phone and shout commands (si no responde, te diré qué hacer; ¡tú, el desfibrilador! ¡tú, a la puerta!)

examples.es: Si no respira, el operador nos dirá cómo hacer las compresiones.
examples.en: If he isn't breathing, the operator will tell us how to do the compressions.

examples.es: ¡Unai, a la puerta! Si llega la ambulancia, la guiarás hasta el campo.
examples.en: Unai, to the gate! If the ambulance arrives, you'll guide it to the pitch.

lessons.title: The Federation Auditor Reviews the Junior Section
lessons.objective: Answer a formal audit on first-aid kits, the concussion log and coaches' certificates, and explain the procedures.

words.note: A man is el auditor.
Here: the required first-aid course certificate.
A woman is la delegada de protección.
A woman is la entrenadora voluntaria.

words.en: Here is this season's concussion log.
words.es: Aquí tiene el registro de conmociones de esta temporada.
words.note: Formal: usted with the auditor.

words.en: Every head knock is logged the same day.
words.es: Cada golpe en la cabeza se registra el mismo día.

words.en: The first-aid kit is checked every month and whatever is missing is replaced.
words.es: El botiquín se revisa cada mes y se repone lo que falta.

words.en: The certificates are filed in each coach's file.
words.es: Los certificados se archivan en el expediente de cada entrenador.

words.en: You're right, one volunteer coach's certificate is missing.
words.es: Tiene razón, falta el certificado de un entrenador voluntario.
words.note: Formal: usted with the auditor.

words.en: What deadline do you give us to hand it in?
words.note: Formal: usted with the auditor.

words.en: Until he hands it in, he won't coach minors.
words.es: Hasta que lo entregue, no entrenará con menores.

words.en: Pedro, can you bring me the first-aid kit inventory, please?
words.es: Pedro, ¿me traes el inventario del botiquín, por favor?
words.note: Informal: tú with a club colleague.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach in charge of the junior section, and the AI is Beatriz Navarro, the federation auditor: walk her through the first-aid kits, the concussion log and the coaches' certificates using formal usted, and explain each procedure with passive se (se registra, se revisa, se archivan).

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se registra cada golpe; se revisa el botiquín; se archivan los certificados)

examples.es: Se revisa la fecha de caducidad de todo el material del botiquín.
examples.en: The expiry date of every item in the first-aid kit is checked.

examples.es: Las autorizaciones de los padres se guardan en la oficina del club.
examples.en: The parental consent forms are kept in the club office.

lessons.title: Write the Weekly Report for the Director of Rugby
lessons.objective: Write a clear weekly report on results, availability, discipline and next week's plan, keeping medical details private.

words.note: Estar de baja = to be out injured or ill. In the report, say who is out, not why.
Written connector that opens a section: En cuanto a la disciplina, ...
Formal written register; followed by a noun or que + clause.

words.en: Regarding results, we won 24-17 at home.
words.es: En cuanto a los resultados, ganamos 24-17 en casa.

words.en: Also, 28 players trained all three days.
words.es: Además, 28 jugadores entrenaron los tres días.

words.en: However, we got two yellow cards for high tackles.
words.es: Sin embargo, recibimos dos tarjetas amarillas por tackles altos.

words.en: Therefore, this week we will work on the low tackle.
words.es: Por lo tanto, esta semana trabajaremos el tackle bajo.

words.en: It is worth noting the debut of two academy players.
words.es: Cabe destacar el debut de dos jugadores de las divisiones formativas.

words.en: Two players are out for Saturday.
words.es: Hay dos jugadores de baja para el sábado.

words.en: I am giving you only availability; the diagnosis is confidential.
words.es: Le indico solo la disponibilidad; el diagnóstico es confidencial.
words.note: Formal (usted), suitable for a written report to the director.

words.en: Without the player's consent, I can't share his diagnosis.
words.es: Sin el consentimiento del jugador, no puedo compartir su diagnóstico.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is director of rugby Santiago Herrera: present your weekly report on results, availability, discipline and next week's plan with en cuanto a, además, sin embargo and por lo tanto, sharing who is available but keeping medical details private.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en cuanto a, además, sin embargo, por lo tanto, cabe destacar)

examples.es: En cuanto a la disponibilidad, Pablo estará de baja dos semanas.
examples.en: Regarding availability, Pablo will be out for two weeks.

examples.es: Sin embargo, mejoramos en el scrum; por lo tanto, mantendremos el plan.
examples.en: However, we improved in the scrum; therefore, we will keep the plan.

lessons.title: Bus Breakdown: Calls and Texts Before Kickoff
lessons.objective: Phone and text the opposition, the referee and the squad politely to move kickoff and change the plan.

words.note: Chile: el bus for a coach; la micro is a city bus.
Chile: quedar en panne = to break down (a vehicle).
Chile says atraso more often than retraso.

words.en: Valentina, I'm writing to let you know we're running late.
words.es: Valentina, te escribo para avisar que tenemos un atraso.
words.note: Informal (tú), normal between team managers by text.

words.en: Could we push the match back an hour?
Mr. Fuentes, would starting at 16:00 work for you?
words.es: Señor Fuentes, ¿le vendría bien empezar a las 16:00?
words.note: Formal (usted) for the referee.

words.en: I left you a voice message; please call me.
words.es: Le dejé un mensaje de voz; llámeme, por favor.
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: Guys, we broke down; nobody get off the bus.
words.es: Cabros, quedamos en panne; nadie se baje del bus.
words.note: Informal Chilean: cabros = guys.

words.en: I'm sharing the live location in the group.
words.es: Les comparto la ubicación en tiempo real en el grupo.

words.en: With the replacement bus, we'd arrive at 15:30.
words.es: Con el bus de reemplazo, llegaríamos a las 15:30.

words.en: I'll confirm the new time as soon as I talk to the referee.
words.es: Te confirmo la nueva hora apenas hable con el árbitro.
words.note: Apenas + subjunctive = as soon as (common in Chile).

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is opposition manager Valentina Soto, then referee Rodrigo Fuentes: explain the bus breakdown, propose a later kickoff with ¿podríamos retrasar...? and ¿le vendría bien...?, then text the squad with les escribo para avisar.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿podríamos retrasar el saque?, te escribo para avisar, ¿le vendría bien...?)

examples.es: ¿Podríamos retrasar el partido media hora?
examples.en: Could we push the match back half an hour?

examples.es: Te escribo para avisar que llegaríamos a las 15:45.
examples.en: I'm writing to let you know we'd arrive at 15:45.

lessons.title: End-of-Season Review with the Board and Sponsor
lessons.objective: Review the season with the president and sponsor and set conditions for next year's plan and budget.

words.note: Meaning 'as long as', it takes the subjunctive: siempre que haya fisio.
Always followed by the subjunctive.

words.en: We stayed up with a very young squad.
words.es: Hemos logrado la permanencia con una plantilla muy joven.

words.en: As long as there is physio, we can fight for promotion.
words.es: Siempre que haya fisioterapia, podremos pelear por el ascenso.

words.en: I would accept other cuts provided there was physio.
words.es: Aceptaría otros recortes con tal de que hubiera fisio.

words.en: Mr. Ortega, I understand the scoreboard interests you.
words.es: Señor Ortega, entiendo que el marcador le interese.
words.note: Formal (usted) for the sponsor.

words.en: Without physio, we would have more injuries and worse results.
words.es: Sin fisio, tendríamos más lesiones y peores resultados.

words.en: Could we fund the scoreboard from another budget line?
words.es: ¿Podríamos financiar el marcador con otra partida presupuestaria?

words.en: I would propose the scoreboard for next season.
words.es: Yo propondría el marcador para la temporada que viene.

words.en: Isabel, shall we take it to the board before deciding?
words.es: Isabel, ¿lo llevamos a la junta directiva antes de decidir?
words.note: Informal (tú), as coach and president often speak in a Spanish club.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI plays president Isabel Castro and sponsor Manuel Ortega: review the season, then set conditions for next year's plan and budget using siempre que, con tal de que and the conditional (propondría, aceptaría).

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (siempre que mantengamos la cantera, renovaríamos; con tal de que haya fisio)

examples.es: Siempre que mantengamos las divisiones formativas, seguiremos creciendo.
examples.en: As long as we keep the academy, we will keep growing.

examples.es: Firmaríamos el presupuesto con tal de que hubiera fisioterapia.
examples.en: We would sign the budget provided there was physiotherapy.

lessons.title: Capstone: Cup Final Day at an Away Ground
lessons.objective: Lead a full cup final day in Spanish, from morning messages to a medical stop, the referee, the commissioner and the report.

words.note: For a woman referee, say la árbitra.

words.en: Heads up: we're arriving 20 minutes late.
words.es: Les aviso: llegamos con 20 minutos de retraso.

words.en: Kevin, get behind the jumper and lift him on the call.
words.es: Kevin, colócate detrás del saltador y levántalo con la llamada.
words.note: Informal (tú) commands with attached pronouns.

words.en: Álvaro, I know you want to carry on, but the doctor decides.
words.es: Álvaro, sé que quieres seguir, pero el médico decide.

words.en: The doctor has taken him off and I back his decision.
words.es: El médico lo ha retirado y yo apoyo su decisión.

words.en: Lorena, could you explain why you gave that penalty?
words.es: Lorena, ¿podría explicarme por qué ha pitado ese golpe?
words.note: Formal (usted) and calm with the referee.

words.en: I'll send you the video and my account tonight.
words.es: Le envío el vídeo y mi versión esta misma noche.
words.note: Formal (usted) for the commissioner.

words.en: Regarding Álvaro, he came off under the concussion protocol.
words.es: En cuanto a Álvaro, salió según el protocolo de conmoción.

words.en: Whatever happens, today we played as a team.
words.es: Pase lo que pase, hoy hemos jugado como un equipo.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI plays everyone at the Segovia cup final: text about the late arrival (les aviso), coach Kevin with levántalo, back the doctor on Álvaro, ask referee Lorena Prieto ¿podría...?, answer the commissioner and dictate the report with en cuanto a.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar

examples.es: Si el médico lo retira, Álvaro no vuelve a entrar, aunque insista.
examples.en: If the doctor takes him off, Álvaro doesn't go back on, even if he insists.

examples.es: Kevin, levántalo cuando oigas la llamada y bájalo despacio.
examples.en: Kevin, lift him when you hear the call and lower him slowly.
